Chapter 3: Why Some Messages Stick—The Secret of Memorable Ideas
Think about your day for a moment. Ads flash by on your phone, friends tell you stories, and headlines crowd your feed. But let’s be honest—most of that stuff? It disappears almost instantly, fading into the background noise of daily life.
Every now and then, though, a message just stands out. It echoes in your mind, pops up in conversations, and somehow finds its way from one person to the next.
So, what actually makes these messages different?
Picture this: there’s a teacher who’s trying everything to help her students remember a tricky lesson. She explains, she repeats, but nothing seems to click. Then one day, she comes up with a short, catchy rhyme that nails the main idea. Suddenly, her students can’t stop saying it! Weeks later, they’re still remembering the lesson—just because of that simple, memorable phrase.
That’s what we call the stickiness factor. It’s the special quality that makes an idea memorable—almost impossible to forget. And here’s what’s interesting: stickiness isn’t about being the loudest or the flashiest. It’s about connecting in a way that just makes sense to people—sometimes tugging at their emotions, sometimes simply making them smile.
Want to see this in action? Let’s look at children’s television. For years, show creators struggled to hold kids’ attention and actually teach them something. They tried all sorts of formats, but most shows just didn’t work. Then, a new style caught on: instead of just dumping information, the shows used repetition, humor, and even invited kids to interact right through the screen.
There was one show that really changed the game. Instead of talking down to kids, it actually paused and waited for them to answer, making each child feel involved. The creators didn’t guess what would work—they tested every part with real kids, tweaking until it was just right. The end result? Kids couldn’t stop watching, and parents couldn’t stop talking about it.
Here’s what we can learn from that: sometimes, it’s the little tweaks in how you share a message that make all the difference. Maybe it’s a story with a clever twist, a slogan that’s easy to repeat, or a picture that grabs your attention. Any of these can make your idea stick.
And it’s not just about having fun. Stickiness matters in serious places too—like health campaigns, classrooms, and businesses. Maybe you’ve seen a health warning that was so technical, you tuned it out. But a simple, bold message? That can actually change what people do. Or think about products—if a name is bland, it might vanish, but a catchy jingle can turn it into something you just can’t forget.
Most people assume that the best ideas win just because they’re good. But let’s face it, how you package and deliver your idea often matters even more. That’s the power of the stickiness factor. It’s what separates messages that disappear from those that spread like wildfire.
So here’s what really matters: focus on the details. Ask yourself—what words will people remember? What images will stay with them? Can you make your message simple, surprising, or even emotionally powerful? By paying attention to these things, you’re much more likely to create ideas that people remember—and love to share.
